# Yugam

> Yugam is an AI transformation consultancy run by Rohit Kumar Maskara (Yugam Systems Pte Ltd, Singapore). Readiness-first consulting for founders and mid-market leadership teams: AI strategy, system architecture, and implementation grounded in how the business actually operates — data, processes, and people before tools.

Rohit Kumar Maskara: a decade at Meta, Fortune 500 governance at KPMG, started on a manufacturing shop floor. B.Tech Industrial Engineering, MBA in Operations Strategy & Finance.

Core position: AI tools are easy to buy. Knowing which ones a business needs — and whether the organization can support them — is the real work. Most AI projects fail for organizational reasons, not technical ones.

## Services

- [How We Work](https://www.yugam.io/#services): Three engagement tiers — Assess (2–4 weeks, readiness audit), Build (8–16 weeks, design and implement), Train (flexible, team enablement)
- [Engagement Methodology](https://www.yugam.io/methodology.html): Phase-by-phase breakdown of how an engagement runs

## Frameworks and articles

- [The 4 Failure Modes That Kill AI Projects](https://www.yugam.io/blog-post-why-ai-deployments-fail.html): Why 70% of AI initiatives fail — a framework for diagnosing organizational readiness before writing code
- [Why 95% of AI Projects Fail to Generate ROI](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-27-why-95-percent-fail.html): Three root causes from major 2026 studies (Deloitte, BCG, HBR, WEF) — all pointing to organizational readiness, not technology
- [How to Spot AI Opportunities in Your Business](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-05-how-to-spot-ai-opportunities.html): Four tests — volume, repeatability, data, cost of error — for finding processes where AI creates value; score by the minimum, not the average
- [How Much Does AI Implementation Cost?](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-05-what-ai-implementation-costs.html): $25K–150K year one for mid-market; the four cost layers and the three patterns that blow up budgets
- [FAQ](https://www.yugam.io/faq.html): Direct answers on AI readiness, costs, timelines, failure causes, tool selection, adoption, and how a Yugam engagement works

## Workflow automation guides

- [What Is AI Workflow Automation?](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-02-what-is-ai-workflow-automation.html): Plain-language guide for executives — what it is, what it does and doesn't do, and the right build sequence
- [The One Workflow Your Team Should Automate First](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-04-first-workflow-to-automate.html): Lead follow-up costs the most hours and loses the most revenue — and it's the easiest to automate well
- [What Is a Workflow Audit?](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-06-what-is-workflow-audit.html): How to map every step in a process before automating anything — skip it and you automate a process you never understood
- [7 Repetitive Workflows Every Service Business Should Automate](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-09-seven-workflows-to-automate.html): Time cost, automation approach, and where to start for the seven biggest time drains
- [How to Automate Business Reporting with AI](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-11-automate-business-reporting.html): Four steps to recover 15–20 hours a month on reporting across a five-person team
- [10 AI Automation Ideas for Consulting Firms](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-13-ai-automation-consulting-firms.html): Ten specific workflows where consulting firms lose hours to manual repetition
- [How to Build an AI-Powered Lead Follow-Up System](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-16-ai-lead-follow-up.html): Six steps to build an automated lead sequence without writing code
- [AI Scheduling Automation for Service Businesses](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-18-ai-scheduling-automation.html): Recover 8–12 hours a month by automating the five scheduling steps that require zero judgment
- [How to Automate Internal Operations](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-20-automate-internal-operations.html): Four workflows worth automating first on teams of 10–30 people
- [AI-Powered Client Onboarding](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-23-ai-client-onboarding.html): Save 5+ hours per new client by mapping and automating predictable onboarding steps
- [How to Automate Customer Support Workflows](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-25-automate-customer-support.html): Automate triage, status updates, and follow-ups — keep humans on the conversations that need judgment
- [AI Workflow Automation: The Complete Guide](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-06-30-complete-automation-guide.html): Strategic framework for service businesses — which workflows to target, how to build them, and common mistakes

## Tool evaluation

- [2026 Guide to Workflow Automation Tools](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-07-workflow-automation-tools-guide.html): Honest evaluation of self-serve platforms, managed services, and custom builds
- [Zapier vs Make: Choosing the Right Platform](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-09-zapier-vs-make.html): Advisory comparison of Zapier, Make, and n8n — which to start with, and when to skip platforms entirely
- [When to Move Beyond Zapier and Make](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-11-beyond-zapier-make.html): Signals that tell you off-the-shelf automation tools are no longer enough
- [What a Good AI Automation Partner Looks Like](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-14-choosing-ai-automation-partner.html): Advisor's checklist for evaluating the 12,000+ automation agencies competing for your attention
- [How to Evaluate AI Automation Vendors](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-16-evaluate-automation-vendors.html): Structured scoring framework across six dimensions with pilot testing protocol
- [Five Questions to Ask Any AI Automation Partner](https://www.yugam.io/resources/article-2026-07-18-questions-for-automation-partner.html): Five questions that separate credible partners from noise — ask before you sign
